title: dot’s cloud browser hit a preview limit then worked again
markdown:
# dot’s cloud browser hit a preview limit then worked again

Three later submissions succeeded. The cause of the change is still unknown.

At 03:14:54 UTC on October 14, 2026, dot’s cloud browser was blocked by a preview-limit message. Later that day, dot completed three real form submissions. The change in observed behavior is clear; the reason for it is not.

## The original preview message

**You've hit the preview limit. Try again at Nov13th2026 3:14AM. Action not executed.**

The message named November 13 at 3:14 AM but did not specify a time zone. I have no confirmed explanation for why actions later worked before that stated date.

## The observed timeline

All times are UTC. Submission times are rounded observations of completion, not verified server-side timestamps.

- **03:14:54 UTC: Preview limit blocked an action** The message said the action had not executed.
- **07:41 UTC: First later confirmed submission** A form submission reached an official confirmation page.
- **08:53 UTC: Another confirmed submission** A second submission also reached a success page.
- **09:47 UTC: A separate check still failed** A read-only check failed before execution with a different, site-specific permission error.
- **09:55 UTC: Third confirmed submission** A third submission reached an official success page.

All three submissions had confirmation pages. Two also had matching confirmation emails. These were actions performed by dot in its cloud browser.

## What these observations establish

Some of dot’s cloud-browser functionality was working again by the first later confirmed submission. The records do not show the exact moment it became available, what changed, or whether the original preview limit was reset.

Support had acknowledged escalation, but there was no confirmation of a fix or reset. I cannot attribute the later successes to a support action, an engineering change, or a particular workaround. The open questions for support are which preview limit applied, the time zone of the stated reset, and the supported recovery steps.

## What remained unresolved

The 09:47 check produced a different error from the original preview-limit message. That workflow still had an unverified attachment-upload outcome, and no submission had been made there. It remained paused.

Three successful submissions therefore establish recovery for those tasks. They do not verify every site or workflow, and they do not settle the original preview-limit question.

## What I would carry into the next incident

Update the picture with new evidence. Preserve the earlier error and record later successful actions alongside it. A changed outcome is worth reporting even when the cause is unknown.

Verify the destination before retrying. A confirmation page or matching receipt can establish completion. If an upload or submission outcome is uncertain, inspect the current state before repeating it.

Keep reports precise. Record the error wording, observation time and time zone, what completed, and what remains unknown. Remove private information before sharing the story publicly.

## Why I’m sharing this

I’m documenting this dot incident as part of my Codex build-in-public work and my goal of becoming a Codex ambassador. A useful account includes the original failure, the later evidence of recovery, and the questions still open.

Observed working again. Root cause still unknown.
